### BEI-01: Risk Awareness Index (Pre)

"On a scale of 1–10, how aware are you of the risks in your life? 1 = I never think about risks. 10 = I know exactly what could go wrong and what I am doing about it."

### INVESTIGATION 1: THE HOOK

MISSION: Meet someone who learned about risk the hard way.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ A prediction about what you would do

TIME: 5 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Observe

### 📖 Read

Episode 1: The SMS That Almost Changed Everything

Meet Thabo.

Thabo is twenty-one. He is in his third year at university. He has a part-time job. He has an online business. He thinks he is financially savvy.

He tracked his time. He saw the leak. He is trying to fix it.

Then he gets an SMS from his "bank." It says: "Suspicious activity detected on your account. Click here to verify your identity or your account will be frozen."

There is a link. It looks legitimate. The sender name is the bank's name.

Thabo almost clicks. He is busy. He is stressed. The message creates urgency.

But something stops him. He remembers: "Banks never ask for your PIN or password via SMS. If you are unsure, call the bank directly—using the number on their website, not the number in the message."

He calls the bank. The fraud department confirms: it is a phishing scam. The link would have taken him to a fake website. If he had entered his credentials, the scammers would have had access to his account. Everything in it—gone.

He almost lost everything. Not because he was stupid. Because the message created urgency. Urgency bypasses your rational brain. It triggers your survival instincts. You act before you question.

He is twenty-one. He almost lost everything. He still has no safety net.

He knows he needs one. He doesn't know how to build it.

### INVESTIGATION 3: THE REVELATION

MISSION: Discover the hidden truth about risk.

YOU WILL PRODUCE:
● ☐ Understanding of risk as probability × magnitude
● ☐ Prediction calibration check

TIME: 3 minutes

DIFFICULTY:           Analyse

### 📖 Read

Episode 2: What Thabo Almost Lost

Thabo almost lost everything. The probability was low. But the magnitude was catastrophic.

Risk is not about what you expect. It is about what you cannot afford.

Most people think risk is about things going wrong. But that is not the right definition. Risk is the probability of loss multiplied by the magnitude of loss.

The phishing SMS was a low-probability event. But if it had worked, the magnitude would have been catastrophic.

Thabo knows he needs protection. He still doesn't know how to build it.

The next day, he walks past the spaza shop. He sees Myah, Sipho, Lethabo, and someone new—an older man named Mr. Patel, who owns a factory. They are building the shelf.

"You're Thabo, right?" Mr. Patel asks. "I heard about what almost happened. What are you doing to protect yourself?"

Thabo thinks. He thinks about his savings. He thinks about his grandmother. He thinks about his lack of a safety net.

"Nothing," he says.

Mr. Patel nods. "I lost everything once. Not a scam. A bad decision. It took me five years to rebuild."

"What did you learn?" Thabo asks.

"Risk is probability times magnitude. The things that could destroy you—insure them. The things that could inconvenience you—accept them. And never make decisions when you're in a hurry."

Thabo nods. He doesn't know if he can do it. But he knows he needs to.

He is twenty-one. He almost lost everything. He still has no safety net.

But he knows what he needs to build.
